note: Student-ready key facts for the Portrait Day design activity. Action lists include major achievements, consequential choices, and important controversies when needed for historical accuracy.

presidents.name: George Washington
presidents.education: No college degree; trained as a surveyor
keyAccomplishments: Created the presidential Cabinet, the president’s group of top advisers
Set the two-term example that later presidents followed
Kept the nation out of war between European powers

importantQuotes.text: The basis of our political systems is the right of the people to make and to alter their constitutions of government.
The Constitution which at any time exists, till changed by an explicit and authentic act of the whole people, is sacredly obligatory upon all.

presentDayConnection.text: Washington stepped down after two terms. The Twenty-Second Amendment later made a two-election limit part of the Constitution.

presidents.name: John Adams
keyAccomplishments: Signed the controversial Alien and Sedition Acts

importantQuotes.text: A government of laws, and not of men.
May none but honest and wise men ever rule under this roof.

presentDayConnection.text: PAST → PRESENT (AS OF JULY 2026): President Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act—one of four laws known together as the Alien and Sedition Acts. Courts have considered how that 1798 wartime law may be used today.

presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
presidents.religion: No official church; influenced by Deism and Unitarian Christianity
keyAccomplishments: Sponsored the Lewis and Clark expedition

importantQuotes.text: We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.
Governments are instituted among Men, deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed.

presidents.name: James Madison
presidents.education: College of New Jersey, now Princeton
keyAccomplishments: Led the country during the War of 1812
Supported rebuilding national money and banking system
Approved the Second Bank of the United States

importantQuotes.text: If men were angels, no government would be necessary.
Justice is the end of government. It is the end of civil society.

presidents.name: James Monroe
presidents.education: College of William and Mary; studied law under Jefferson

importantQuotes.text: National honor is national property of the highest value.
Let us by all wise and constitutional measures promote intelligence among the people as the best means of preserving our liberties.

presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
keyAccomplishments: Promoted roads, canals, science, and education

importantQuotes.text: But she goes not abroad, in search of monsters to destroy.
She is the well-wisher to the freedom and independence of all.

presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
presidents.birthplace: South Carolina (claimed; the exact state is disputed)
keyAccomplishments: Enforced the destructive Indian Removal policy

importantQuotes.text: Our Federal Union: It must be preserved.
That this was intended to be a government of limited and specific, and not general, powers must be admitted by all.
I bring with me a settled purpose to maintain the institutions of my country.
Conscious of but one desire, faithfully to serve my country, I throw myself without fear on its justice and its kindness.

presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
presidents.education: Hampden-Sydney College and medical study at Pennsylvania; no degree
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Army officer, territorial governor, and U.S. senator
keyAccomplishments: His death tested rules for replacing a president

importantQuotes.text: The only legitimate right to govern is an express grant of power from the governed.
The Constitution of the United States is the instrument containing this grant of power to the several departments composing the Government.

presidents.name: John Tyler
keyAccomplishments: Established that the vice president fully becomes president
Supported adding Texas to the United States
Broke with his own Whig Party

importantQuotes.text: This same occurrence has subjected the wisdom and sufficiency of our institutions to a new test.
I shall place in the intelligence and patriotism of the people my only sure reliance.

presidents.name: James K. Polk
keyAccomplishments: Expanded U.S. territory after the Mexican-American War

importantQuotes.text: The Constitution itself...will be the chart by which I shall be directed.
The Government of the United States is one of delegated and limited powers.

presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
presidents.education: Limited formal schooling; career military training
keyAccomplishments: Opposed expanding slavery into western territories

importantQuotes.text: In the discharge of these duties my guide will be the Constitution.
To exhaust every resort of honorable diplomacy before appealing to arms.

presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
keyAccomplishments: Sent the expedition that opened relations with Japan

importantQuotes.text: The Constitution has made it the duty of the President to take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
In a government like ours, all laws are passed by a majority of the representatives of the people.

presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
keyAccomplishments: Saw violent conflict between the North and South intensify

importantQuotes.text: The dangers of a concentration of all power in the general government of a confederacy so vast as ours are too obvious to be disregarded.
Beautiful as our fabric is, no earthly power or wisdom could ever reunite its broken fragments.

presidents.name: James Buchanan
keyAccomplishments: Failed to stop the crisis over states leaving the United States
Remained in office as seven states left the United States

importantQuotes.text: Our own country could alone have exhibited so grand and striking a spectacle of the capacity of man for self-government.
May we not, then, hope that the long agitation on this subject is approaching its end?

presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
presidents.education: About one year of formal schooling; self-educated in law

importantQuotes.text: A house divided against itself cannot stand.
With malice toward none, with charity for all.
The message or declaration must be made by the acts as they transpire.
Duties have been mine; consequences are God's.

presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
presidents.education: United States Military Academy at West Point
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Army officer and commanding general of the U.S. Army
keyAccomplishments: Enforced civil rights during Reconstruction, the effort to rebuild after the Civil War

importantQuotes.text: Let us have peace.
The question of suffrage is one which is likely to agitate the public so long as a portion of the citizens of the nation are excluded from its privileges.

presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
presidents.education: Kenyon College and Harvard Law School
keyAccomplishments: Promoted civil-service reform, or government hiring based on skill
Withdrew federal troops from the South

importantQuotes.text: He serves his party best who serves the country best.
The permanent pacification of the country upon such principles and by such measures as will secure the complete protection of all its citizens.

presidents.name: James A. Garfield
keyAccomplishments: Challenged the patronage system of giving government jobs to political supporters
Defended federal education and civil rights
Was assassinated months after taking office

importantQuotes.text: The Constitution guarantees absolute religious freedom.
The elevation of the Negro race from slavery to the full rights of citizenship is the most important political change we have known since the adoption of the Constitution.

presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
keyAccomplishments: Signed the Pendleton Civil Service Act

importantQuotes.text: The wisdom of our fathers, foreseeing even the most dire possibilities, made sure that the Government should never be imperiled because of the uncertainty of human life.
Men may die, but the fabrics of our free institutions remain unshaken.

presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
keyAccomplishments: Used the veto more than earlier presidents

importantQuotes.text: Public office is a public trust.
He mocks the people who proposes that the Government shall protect the rich and that they in turn will care for the laboring poor.
The oath taken in the presence of the people becomes a mutual covenant.
The whole body of the people covenant with me and with each other to-day to support and defend the Constitution and the Union of the States.

presidents.name: William McKinley
presidents.education: Allegheny College and Albany Law School; no degree
keyAccomplishments: Led the nation in the Spanish-American War

importantQuotes.text: Our differences are policies; our agreements, principles.
The people themselves, not their servants, can safely reverse their own deliberate judgment.

presidents.name: Theodore Roosevelt
presidents.education: Harvard College; attended Columbia Law School
keyAccomplishments: Advanced construction of the Panama Canal

importantQuotes.text: The first requisite of a good citizen in this Republic of ours is that he shall be able and willing to pull his weight.
Speak softly and carry a big stick; you will go far.

presidents.name: William Howard Taft
presidents.education: Yale College and Cincinnati Law School
keyAccomplishments: Filed major antitrust, or anti-monopoly cases

importantQuotes.text: Our international policy is always to promote peace.
The welfare of the farmer is vital to that of the whole country.

presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
presidents.education: Princeton University and Johns Hopkins University; attended Virginia Law
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Lawyer, Professor, College Administrator, Public Official
keyAccomplishments: Created the Federal Reserve, the nation’s central banking system
Led the nation during World War I
Promoted the League of Nations while separating federal workers by race

importantQuotes.text: Justice, and only justice, shall always be our motto.
The firm basis of government is justice, not pity.

presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
keyAccomplishments: Supported treaties that limited weapons after World War I
His administration was damaged by major scandals

importantQuotes.text: America's present need is not heroics, but healing; not nostrums, but normalcy; not revolution, but restoration.
I accept my part with single-mindedness of purpose and humility of spirit.
The chief business of the American people is business.
The government of a country never gets ahead of the religion of a country.

presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
keyAccomplishments: Expanded public works during the Depression
Failed to stop the economic collapse

importantQuotes.text: Absolute freedom of the press to discuss public questions is a foundation stone of American liberty.
We in America today are nearer to the final triumph over poverty than ever before in the history of any land.

presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
presidents.education: Harvard College; attended Columbia Law School
keyAccomplishments: Created New Deal relief and reform programs
Led the nation through most of World War II
Ordered the incarceration of Japanese Americans

importantQuotes.text: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
The measure of the restoration lies in the extent to which we apply social values more noble than mere monetary profit.

presentDayConnection.text: Roosevelt’s order incarcerating Japanese Americans remains a warning about civil liberties during a crisis. In 2018, the Supreme Court said Korematsu was gravely wrong.

presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
presidents.education: High school; attended business and law courses without a degree
keyAccomplishments: Approved the Marshall Plan and NATO

importantQuotes.text: The buck stops here.
Democracy is based on the conviction that man has the moral and intellectual capacity, as well as the inalienable right, to govern himself with reason and justice.

presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
presidents.education: United States Military Academy at West Point
keyAccomplishments: Created the Interstate Highway System, the national network of major highways
Enforced school desegregation in Little Rock
Warned about the close relationship between the military, government, and defense companies

importantQuotes.text: In the councils of government, we must guard against the acquisition of unwarranted influence, whether sought or unsought, by the military-industrial complex.
The potential for the disastrous rise of misplaced power exists and will persist.

presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Writer, Navy Officer, Journalist, Public Official
keyAccomplishments: Committed the nation to a Moon landing

importantQuotes.text: Ask not what your country can do for you—ask what you can do for your country.
We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard.

presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
keyAccomplishments: Signed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts

importantQuotes.text: We shall overcome.
The vote is the most powerful instrument ever devised by man for breaking down injustice.

presidents.name: Richard Nixon
presidents.education: Whittier College and Duke Law School

importantQuotes.text: The greatest honor history can bestow is the title of peacemaker.
We cannot learn from one another until we stop shouting at one another.

presidents.name: Gerald Ford
presidents.education: University of Michigan and Yale Law School

importantQuotes.text: Our long national nightmare is over.
Our Constitution works; our great Republic is a government of laws and not of men.

presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Farmer, Navy Officer, Public Official, Professor
keyAccomplishments: Made human rights central to foreign policy

importantQuotes.text: Our Government must at the same time be both competent and compassionate.
The powerful must not persecute the weak, and human dignity must be enhanced.

presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
keyAccomplishments: Negotiated arms reductions with the Soviet Union

importantQuotes.text: In this present crisis, government is not the solution to our problem; government is the problem.
Government can and must provide opportunity, not smother it.

presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
keyAccomplishments: Led the coalition in the Gulf War
Signed the Americans with Disabilities Act
Managed the end of the Cold War

importantQuotes.text: There is but one just use of power, and it is to serve people.
A new breeze is blowing, and a world refreshed by freedom seems reborn.

presidents.name: Bill Clinton
presidents.education: Georgetown University, Oxford University, and Yale Law School
keyAccomplishments: Presided over economic growth and budget surpluses
Was impeached by the House but not removed by the Senate

importantQuotes.text: Our democracy must be not only the envy of the world but the engine of our own renewal.
There is nothing wrong with America that cannot be cured by what is right with America.

presidents.name: George W. Bush
presidents.education: Yale University and Harvard Business School
keyAccomplishments: Led the response to the September 11 attacks
Launched wars in Afghanistan and Iraq

importantQuotes.text: Freedom itself was attacked this morning by a faceless coward, and freedom will be defended.
America has never been united by blood or birth or soil. We are bound by ideals that move us beyond our backgrounds.

presidents.name: Barack Obama
presidents.education: Occidental College, Columbia University, and Harvard Law School
keyAccomplishments: Led recovery from the Great Recession

importantQuotes.text: On this day, we gather because we have chosen hope over fear, unity of purpose over conflict and discord.
We reject as false the choice between our safety and our ideals.

presidents.name: Donald Trump
presidents.education: Fordham University and University of Pennsylvania
presidents.careerBeforePresidency: Real Estate Businessman and Reality TV Personality

importantQuotes.text: The forgotten men and women of our country will be forgotten no longer.
What truly matters is not which party controls our government, but whether our government is controlled by the people.

presidents.name: Joe Biden
presidents.education: University of Delaware and Syracuse University College of Law
keyAccomplishments: Signed major infrastructure and climate legislation
Signed the CHIPS and Science Act

importantQuotes.text: This is America’s day. This is democracy’s day.
We must end this uncivil war that pits red against blue.
